meta.title: Seats that move under the proposed rule, 2030
meta.subtitle: 3 seats would move between 6 states
meta.coordinateSpace: Pixels in a 1152 x 748.8 frame, y increasing downward. Ready for SVG.
meta.method: Each state is carved into max(seatsFrom, seatsTo) equal-area cells, so every cell in the country is the same size and a state is drawn at its peak seat count. |change| cells are marked as the seats that moved.
meta.cellChoice: A seat is apportioned to a state, not to a place within it, so which cell carries the mark is presentational, not a claim about where a seat was won or lost. Rule: start from the cell whose seed lies furthest from the state centroid, so change reads at the margin; restrict to the state's largest landmass where that is distinguishable; and for a multi-seat change grow the block by nearest neighbour so it reads as one group. Note that New York's marked cell lands on Long Island, which sits visually close to Connecticut even though it is inside New York's outline. Marked lost cells have no district id.
meta.rule: 15 CFR part 60 as proposed at 91 FR 57524 (Sept. 10, 2026). Proposed sec. 60.4 counts foreign citizens who are 'either citizens or lawful permanent residents of the United States' and directs that all others are 'not counted for apportionment.' Both columns are projections to 2030 on the same recency-weighted basis; neither is a result.
meta.source: Apportionment by Jonathan Cervas, Carnegie Mellon University. Population: Census Bureau vintage 2025 estimates projected to 2030; composition from ACS 1-year 2005-2024; lawful permanent residents from DHS OHSS.
